newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK boatpeople issue won't be resolved by handover - UN.
newsitem.headline: HK boatpeople issue won't be resolved by handover - UN.

text.p: Hong Kong will not be able to meet Beijing's deadline to clear the last Vietnamese boatpeople from detention camps before China takes back the territory on July 1, a senior United Nations offical said on Friday.

Sergio Vieira de Mello, Assistant High Commissioner for Refugees, told a news conference that about 1,500 asylum-seekers would still be in Hong Kong after the handover to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
Of the asylum-seekers who would remain, 1,000 were determined to be refugees and the other 500 were deemed illegal immigrants, Vieira de Mello said.
Vieira de Mello made the comments after meeting British Governor Chris Patten, legislators, and immigration and security officials during his two-day visit to the territory.

"Unless a miracle can be produced by June 30, we are likely to be left with a few hundreds of individuals in Hong Kong which I believe it is not something that should cause concern to the (post-handover) government and to Beijing," he said.
China has repeatedly told Britain and Hong Kong's colonial administration that the Whitehead and High Island detention camps must be emptied by the handover.
He said the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees could not set a timetable for when the 1,500 would leave Hong Kong.
"It will depend on the generosity of recipient countries," he said of those in the refugee category.
The departure dates of those classified as illegal immigrants would depend on agreement between the Vietnamese and Hong Kong governments over repatriation flights.
But Vieira de Mello acknowledged that many countries which in the past had granted asylum to Vietnamese boatpeople were now feeling over-burdened.

"Burnout, definitely. How much longer can we expect these countries to continue to display generosity towards...the Vietnamese?" he said. "But our message to them will be that we have come to an end of the long, tragic saga."
Vieira de Mello, who will visit Beijing on Sunday, said he would discuss the boatpeople issue with Chinese authorities along with other matters.
Currently there are 2,700 boatpeople in Hong Kong detention camps. Another 1,300 are being cleared as genuine refugees and are awaiting asylum in third countries.
The boatpeople are the last of a human tide of tens of thousands who have fled their homeland since the communists won the Vietnam War in 1975.
